source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 8.

sections.heading: 1. Measuring Time
points: Early people measured time using **repeating natural events** — day/night, Moon phases, seasons.
Early devices: **sundial, water clock, sand clock (hourglass)**.
**Galileo** discovered the steady swing of a **pendulum**, leading to **pendulum clocks**; modern clocks use **quartz** (very accurate).
**SI unit of time = second (s)**; 1 minute = 60 s, 1 hour = 3600 s.

sections.heading: 2. The Simple Pendulum
points: A **simple pendulum** = a bob hung by a thread from a fixed point.
One complete to-and-fro swing = one **oscillation**.
**Time period** = time for **one oscillation**; it is **constant** for a given pendulum and depends on its **length** (not the bob's mass).

sections.heading: 3. Motion and Speed
points: **Motion** = change of position with time; may be **uniform** (constant speed) or **non-uniform**.
**Speed = Distance ÷ Time**; SI unit = **metre per second (m/s)** (also km/h).
**Speedometer** measures speed; **odometer** measures distance travelled.

sections.heading: 4. Distance–Time Graphs
points: Plot **time on the x-axis** and **distance on the y-axis**.
A **straight sloping line** = **uniform motion**; a **horizontal line** = object **at rest**; a **curve** = non-uniform motion.
The **steeper** the line, the **greater** the speed.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: SI unit of time = second; early clocks: sundial, water clock, sand clock.
Galileo → pendulum; time period depends on length, not mass.
Speed = distance ÷ time; SI unit = m/s; speedometer = speed, odometer = distance.
Oscillation = one to-and-fro swing; time period = time for one oscillation (constant).
Distance–time graph: straight line = uniform; horizontal = at rest; steeper = faster.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **SI unit of time = second**; **SI unit of speed = m/s**.
A pendulum's **time period** depends on its **length**, not the bob's mass.
**Speedometer** = speed; **odometer** = distance — don't swap.
On a distance–time graph, a **horizontal** line = **at rest** (not fastest).
